Treatment summary
Patient presented following a low-speed head-on motor vehicle collision with complaints of neck and low back pain, muscle
tightness, and reduced range of motion. The reported mechanism of injury is consistent with the force of the clolision and with
the symptoms described. Cervical and lumbar paraspinal tenderness and restricted active motion were documented on
examination, while neurological screening, reflexes, and motor strength remained within normal limits. The patient has no known
prior injury or treatment involving the cervical or lumbar spine. Care was delivered over 21 visits, which is somewhat longer than
typical for uncomplicated cervical and lumbar strain, and included manual therapy, therapeutic exercise, and home exercise
instruction. Progress has been gradual, with improvement in pain scores and mobility over the course of treatment. Billed
services reviewed for this episode show no duplicated or repeated charges. Ongoing care will focus on strengthening and a
graded return to usual activities, with reassessment planned at discharge.
</page>

Rate each feature below that THIS page gives evidence about. Leave out a feature the page
says nothing about. The ratings are listed from least to most suspicious.
- injury_crash_fit: Does the claimed injury fit the type and force of the crash? Allowed: Strong, Reasonable, Unclear, Inconsistent.
- treatment_growth: Did the treatment grow beyond what this injury needs? Allowed: Normal, Elevated, Disproportionate, Extreme.
- objective_support: Do objective tests (imaging, exam findings) support the complaints? Allowed: Strong, Partial, Predominantly subjective, Contradicted.
- pre_existing_condition: Did an earlier condition of the same body area add to the complaints? Allowed: None, Minor, Material, Predominant.
- duplicate_billing: Was the same service, visit or part billed twice? Allowed: None, Possible, Confirmed.

For each rated feature give:
- "rating": exactly one of the allowed ratings,
- "confidence": "High", "Medium" or "Low" (how clearly the page shows it),
- "quote": one or two sentences copied EXACTLY from the page that support the rating, with any
  spelling errors as they are,
- "reason": one short sentence.
